catalog_locator: Kap. II, § 39 'A. Den exspiratoriska akcenten', pp. 56-57; § 40 (musical accent); § 42 Anm. 3 (compound exceptions)
catalog_quote: § 39. A. Den exspiratoriska akcenten. Målet har uppgivit skillnaden mellan akut ock grav ock endast behållit den förra akcentformen. Huvudtonen vilar i regeln på första stavelsen i ordet ock utmärkes i detta fall icke av mig genom något särskilt tecken. Undantag bilda endast en del sammansatta ord, varom se § 42, anm. 3, ävensom några vanligen hsv. lånord med obetonade prefix, t. ex. ... betala ... förklara ... Lånord sådana som de följande lyda huvudregeln ock ha alltså tonen på första stavelsen: baron ... kopek ... parti ... kvartér ... butelj. Märk, att dessa ord förete liknande former i estn., där samma regel om akcent på första stavelsen råder. ... Stark biton. I de sammansättningar, vars första led är huvudtonig, är första stavelsen i senare leden, resp. en av de senare lederna så starkt betonad, att denna biton nära nog väger upp huvudtonen. ... Svagton. Under denna tärm sammanfa…

new_statements.quote: Simplex words in Swedish have one word stress, compounds typically two stresses: a primary stress on the first, and a secondary stress on the final element of the compound. (p. 343) | ES has been characterised as only having one kind of word accent (e.g. Haugen, 1976) [...] ES dialects have lost the accents under the influence of Estonian (Lagman, 1979: 38). (p. 344) | the contour for Type 1 compounds (simplex word accent) has a word-initial peak aligned with the primary stressed vowel followed by a fall throughout the word. [...] all the words were produced with a clear primary stress, while the secondary stress was not phonetically realised. (p. 346)

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's fixed: initial syllable record (initial stress): primary stress on the first element/first syllable in the compound data, with secondary stress on the final element. Adds compound-level detail (four Lagman compound-accent types, two of which are exceptions: word-group accent with two primary stresses and final-element stress) and the statement that the Swedish tonal accent distinction has been lost in ES. Does not state a placement rule for simplex words.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The paper is an acoustic study of pitch (tonal word accent) in Estonian Swedish compounds, not a statement of word-stress placement, and it explicitly leaves simplex-word accentuation for future work (p. 351). What it does say: the general Swedish frame it works in has one word stress per simplex word and, in compounds, primary stress on the first element with secondary stress on the final element (p. 343); ES compound Types 1 and 2 show a single early F0 peak aligned with the primary stressed vowel of the first element (pp. 346-347); ES has lost the Swedish Accent 1/Accent 2 tonal opposition under Estonian influence, so there is no tonal word-accent contrast (p. 344). This is compatible with the catalog's initial-stress record but does not independently state a rule for simplex words.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In compounds, secondary stress on the final element (p. 343); in Type 1 ('simplex word accent') compounds such as heimgiod, tolemod the secondary stress was not phonetically realised (p. 346); in Type 2 ('compound accent') compounds the contour is a single early peak with no tonal synchronisation on the secondary stress (pp. 346-347).
new_statements.exceptions: Two compound types deviate from first-element primary stress: Type 3 'word group accent' (ordgruppsaccent), where per Lagman (1979: 24) both (or all) elements are pronounced with the primary stress, e.g. korngrins korvar, klimp supp, acoustically double-peaked (p. 348); and Type 4 'final element stress' (efterledsbetoning), only two tokens tole-sa 'such a' and håla-mod 'in which way', with a low first element and the peak on the stressed syllable of the second element (p. 348). The read-sentence stimuli are transcribed [ˈbiːlˌbranɧən] and [mʊˈbiːltɛlɛˌfoːnən] (p. 345-346), i.e. the loan compound mobiltelefonen carries non-initial primary stress on -bil-, as in Standard Swedish.
new_statements.identity_note: The 2013 paper's data are from the Rickul variety of Estonian Swedish (Rickul lies in Nuckö parish, so this is the Nuckömålet area): Edvin Lagman and his 79-year-old mother recorded in 1965 (63 compounds), plus four elderly Rickul speakers recorded in Stockholm in 2009 reading Swedish sentences (p. 345). The paper notes that compound accentuation may differ between ES dialects (p. 351, citing Lagman 1979). A second paper by the same authors, Schötz & Asu 2015 'In search of word accents in Estonian Swedish' (ICPhS 0314), was already held by the project in the same folder from an earlier reading; it likewise concerns the Accent 1/2 tonal question and was not in the works list, so it is not reported as a works entry.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is present verbatim in the held Danell 1905 djvu text at § 39, with the p.56/57 break exactly where the locator says; § 40 and § 42 Anm. 3 also verified. (2) Deciding source: a 1905 Uppsala doctoral dissertation that is a full phonology monograph of this very dialect, by a professional dialectologist; Glottolog has no descriptive references at all for esto1259, and no later reference grammar or phonology of Nuckömålet supersedes it. A second, independent held primary source (Vendell 1881 §§ 50-51, pp. 67-68) states the same rule ('gesetzmässig auf der ersten Sylbe.. selbst wenn zusammengesetzt'; musical accent 'blos akut'). The modern instrumental literature (Schötz & Asu 2015, downloaded now; 2013 on compounds, paywalled) works on tonal accent and compound accentuation in Ormsö-Nuckö-Rickul speech and is consistent with Danell: no Accent 1/2 contra

sources.citation: Schötz, Susanne & Eva Liina Asu. 2015. In search of word accents in Estonian Swedish. Proceedings of the 18th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences (ICPhS 2015), Glasgow, paper 0314.
sources.quote: Instrumental F0 study of 'disyllabic simplex words with stress on the penult' (i.e. initial stress in disyllables, taken as given); 'In traditional accounts, ES is characterised as only having one kind of word accent'; conclusion: 'it can be concluded that Estonian Swedish does not have a word accent distinction ... ES can be placed as a Type 0 variety alongside Finland Swedish'. Cites Schötz & Asu 2013 for compound accentuation resembling Finland Swedish.
sources.locator: Abstract and §1 (p.1), §5 Conclusion (p.4); nine speakers of the Ormsö-Nuckö-Rickul dialect recorded 2008-2014

sources.note: Only instrumental study of stress/accent distribution in Estonian Swedish (Ormsö-Nuckö) compounds; would put measurements behind our the secondary-stress rule ('stark biton' on later compound members nearly equal to main stress) and Danell's § 42 Anm. 3 compound exceptions. Does not bear on the primary 'initial stress' coding.

sources.note: The standard 20th-century overview of all Estonian Swedish dialects (the source Schötz & Asu cite for ES having a single word accent and for inter-dialect differences); would confirm that Danell's Nuckö rule holds across the esto1259 umbrella (Ormsö, Rågö, Runö, Dagö, Nargö) rather than for Nuckö alone.
